newsitem.title: USA: Housing aid needed under U.S. welfare law-groups.
newsitem.headline: Housing aid needed under U.S. welfare law-groups.

text.p: More than 50 advocacy groups asked Congress and the White House Wednesday to increase housing subsidies for the poor as they work out a 1998 budget, saying aid was vital to making a new welfare law work.

The groups, including the National Association of Counties, National League of Cities and National Urban League charged that far-reaching state welfare changes were already increasingly homelessness in some areas of the United States.
They warned a new federal welfare law giving states new authority and limiting cash aid to five years could make the problem worse.
"If we want people to get off welfare and go to work, we need to provide housing for them," Cushing Dolbeare, founder of the National Low Income Housing Coalition, said in a statement.
"This is a time when HUD should be providing more housing, not reducing the number of families who need help," he said.
The groups cited a December 13 Housing and Urban Development report said HUD would need an additional $2.3 billion between 1997 and 2002 to meet current commitments for housing aid.
Press reports last month suggested the White House wanted to cut HUD's budget by $1 billion and give states federal funds in the form of block grants.

Congress has reduced housing aid during the past two years. About 1.5 of 4.5 milllion people who receive housing aid receive either cash welfare or federal disability aid. Both are being reduced under the welfare law.
